title: How does a dollar bill get made?
sources: Bureau of Engraving and Printing Currency Production

lines.text: Did you know that American dollar bills are not actually made out of paper?
lines.caps: Dollar bills are *not | made out of *paper!

lines.text: If they were made of wood pulp paper, a single accidental trip through the laundry washing machine would turn them into mush.
lines.caps: Wood paper would turn to *mush | in your *washing machine

lines.text: U.S. currency is printed on a unique blend of seventy-five percent cotton and twenty-five percent linen.
Tiny red and blue synthetic fibers are woven directly into the fabric to defeat counterfeiters.
lines.caps: Tiny red and blue *threads | are woven into the *fabric

lines.text: Giant intaglio printing presses stamp sheets under twenty tons of pressure, creating raised ink textures you can feel with your fingernail.
lines.caps: Intaglio presses apply *20 tons | of pressure for raised *ink

lines.text: Color-shifting bells and 3D security ribbons turn bills into high-tech security sheets.
A dollar bill can be folded over four thousand times before it finally tears.
lines.caps: Can be folded *4,000 times | before ever *ripping!
